turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Madam, I have taken the vitals. Blood pressure is 142 over 88, pulse 78, temperature 36.8, oxygen 98 percent.
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry doctor, we got late. The auto was stuck near the sabzi market.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): That is fine. Sit, both of you. What brings you?
[SEG0004] person_4 (PATIENT): Doctor, I have high BP since many years, but today I came for this pain. Right upper stomach, it comes after fatty meals, and it stays two or three hours.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mm. We will come to the pressure. Since when is this pain?
[SEG0006] person_4 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Umm, maybe three weeks, I cannot say the day. It has come two or three times, only when the food is oily.
[SEG0007] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Worst was the wedding biryani. She would not even lie down, just sat holding her side.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Did you vomit that night?
[SEG0009] person_4 (PATIENT): Once only. I vomited. Not again after that.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0011] person_4 (PATIENT): No. No fever.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yellow in the eyes, or the urine turning dark?
[SEG0013] person_4 (PATIENT): Not really.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Loose motions?
[SEG0015] person_4 (PATIENT): Never. Motions are normal only.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Does the pain go to the shoulder or the back?
[SEG0017] person_4 (PATIENT): No. It stays here only.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Which tablets are you on?
[SEG0019] person_4 (PATIENT): Digene, uh, the white chewable ones, two tablets when the pain starts. And for pressure, my BP tablet, amlodopin, five milligram, one every morning.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any medicine allergy?
[SEG0021] person_4 (PATIENT): No. Nothing.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any operation in the past?
[SEG0023] person_4 (PATIENT): Never. Is it something bad? I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me press here. Tender under the right ribs. The belly is soft, no guarding. Eyes are not yellow.
[SEG0025] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Her mother had the gallbladder surgery for stones, years back. She is thinking it is the same.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): That is useful. With your blood pressure, any chest pain?
[SEG0027] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): And shortness of breath?
[SEG0029] person_4 (PATIENT): No... well, sometimes. Climbing stairs, a little. I don't know, doctor, whether it is the pressure.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Swelling in the feet?
[SEG0031] person_4 (PATIENT): Not that either. Feet are fine.

[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Err, thinking aloud. Right upper pain after oily food, for hours, mother had stones. I am keeping gallstones with biliary colic, and also simple gastritis, both open. I will not conclude which today.
[SEG0033] person_4 (PATIENT): Gallbladder, like my mother? I am scared, I don't know.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am not saying it is that for certain. Heart pain is less likely, but I will not rule it out fully. We will see what the tests say.
[SEG0035] person_4 (PATIENT): Ok doctor. What to do?
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am booking blood tests, liver function, full blood count and serum amylase. And an ultrasound of the abdomen, for this week.
[SEG0037] person_4 (PATIENT): The scan, will it pain? I don't know, doctor.

[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): No pain from the scan. Avoid oily and fried food, and continue Digene when the pain comes. Come back in one week with the reports. If the pain comes with fever or you vomit again, come earlier, do not wait.

spec.situation: Woman with right-upper stomach pain after fatty meals, lasting hours, once with vomiting; takes antacid; mother had gallbladder surgery; blood tests and ultrasound planned.

traps.happens: The patient denies some symptoms (said as 'no', 'not really', 'never'), has a chronic condition named earlier (for example asthma or hypertension) and later the doctor asks about another symptom of it, and one answer is a double negative or a correction ('not that either', 'no... well, sometimes').
traps.label_rule: Denials go in negative_findings with the exact thing denied, never in symptoms. NEVER write a negative about a condition the patient has said they have. A corrected answer keeps only the final version. A negative is never a symptom, and 'not painful' is the finding 'pain' absent, not a symptom called 'painless'.

features: colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
